name: Tidio
tagline: A live chat and helpdesk suite where the Lyro AI agent reportedly handles about 90% of conversations on its own.
tldr: Tidio is a live chat, helpdesk, and AI chatbot platform built primarily for e-commerce and small-to-mid-sized business websites, centered on its Lyro AI Agent.

Pricing separates the core helpdesk (Free through Plus/Premium, based on billable conversations and seats) from Lyro AI Agent conversations and Flows (rule-based automation), which are billed as add-ons starting around $32.50/mo for 50+ Lyro conversations.
Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Szczecin, Poland, Tidio has raised roughly $26.8M through a 2022 Series B round and runs a lean team of around 178 employees.

Independent reviews are strong across major review platforms, with reviewers citing minimal AI hallucination and around 90% of conversations resolved by Lyro, but pricing transparency (unexpected plan upgrades, refund friction) is the single most-cited complaint.
A notable product limitation: you can't blend a simple rule-based bot with intelligent Lyro AI handoff in one flow — it's a binary choice between a scripted bot and the full AI agent.
keyFeatures: Lyro AI Agent that autonomously resolves customer conversations, trained on a store/site's own content and continuously refined for accuracy
Live chat widget with ticketing and email management bundled into the base plan, even at the Free tier
Flows — a separate rule-based automation product for triggered messages and simple scripted bots, billed independently from Lyro
Automatic chat assignment, macros, and granular permissions from the Growth tier upward
Guaranteed 50% Lyro AI resolution rate on the Premium tier, with pay-per-resolution billing as an alternative to flat conversation packs
Dedicated Success Manager, custom branding, multiproject support, and OpenAPI access on the Plus tier
SSO, managed service, and compliance features (Slack support, security controls) reserved for Premium/Enterprise
E-commerce platform integrations designed for online store support and sales-assist use cases

faq.question: How is Tidio's pricing structured?
faq.answer: The core helpdesk (live chat, ticketing, email) is priced by billable conversations and seats — Free (50 conversations, 10 seats), Starter (~$24/mo, 100 conversations), Growth (~$49/mo, up to 2,000 conversations). Lyro AI Agent conversations and Flows are billed as separate add-ons on top, starting around $32.50/mo for 50+ Lyro conversations.

faq.question: How good is the Lyro AI agent in practice?
faq.answer: Independent reviews report roughly 90% of conversations resolved by Lyro with minimal hallucination, and G2 reviewers note the AI's responses have become more accurate and natural over time as Tidio has refined the model.

faq.question: Can I mix a simple scripted bot with Lyro AI handoff?
faq.answer: Not smoothly — reviewers flag this as a real limitation. The platform currently forces a fairly rigid choice between a simple rule-based bot (Flows) and the full Lyro AI agent, rather than letting a scripted bot intelligently escalate to AI mid-conversation.

faq.question: What's the most common complaint about Tidio?
faq.answer: Pricing transparency — specifically automatic plan upgrades happening without clear permission and difficulty securing refunds afterward — is the most frequently repeated complaint across independent reviews.

faq.question: Is Tidio a good fit for e-commerce specifically?
faq.answer: Yes — it's built with e-commerce integrations and sales-assist use cases in mind, and is frequently compared against Chatbase and Crisp as a budget-to-mid-tier option for online stores wanting AI-assisted support.

criteriaScores.note: Covers web chat, email, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Instagram DM, and Telegram (tidio.com/multichannel, help.tidio.com Channels section), but there's no native voice channel and SMS is not a first-class Tidio channel the way it is on Crisp or ManyChat.

Tidio's own shared-inbox documentation states that if a customer messages on Instagram and follows up by email, the agent sees both in the same thread with full history and customer sidebar (tidio.com/shared-inbox).

Lyro is a genuine generative AI agent (not canned replies) that Tidio confirms runs on a Claude-based LLM, per Tidio's own Lyro documentation and multiple third-party writeups (help.tidio.com, tidio.com/blog/lyro-review).

G2 reviewers (4.6/5 aggregate, ~1,900+ reviews) frequently praise Lyro's accuracy and speed, but the specific ~90% resolution figure traces mainly to Tidio's own blog/marketing rather than an independent audit, so it should be treated as vendor-influenced even though reviewer sentiment is genuinely positive.

Lyro auto-scrapes website content into Q&A pairs, supports Zendesk help-center import, file upload (Plus plan), and suggests Q&As from historical conversations — all documented in Tidio's help center (Data sources - Lyro's knowledge base).

Lyro is bounded to ingested knowledge-base content and escalates unanswerable questions to a human; G2 reviewers report that deliberate attempts to make it hallucinate false info were unsuccessful, per Tidio's Lyro review page and G2 review mining.

Flows is a genuine visual, drag-and-drop rule-based builder with branching/conditional logic and 40+ templates (tidio.com/flows), but it runs as a separate product from Lyro AI rather than one blended agentic workflow — reviewers specifically flag the lack of smooth AI-to-scripted-bot handoff.

Lyro Guidance lets you configure escalation on detected anger/frustration or specific keywords, and Lyro parses question intent to select the right knowledge (help.tidio.com Lyro Guidance), though some independent comparisons note it lacks the deeper sentiment analytics of dedicated CX platforms.

Tidio's Inbox documentation describes a single interface aggregating live chat, tickets, and all connected channels with one customer profile sidebar showing contact details, location, and history (help.tidio.com, The Inbox article).

When Lyro hits its knowledge limits or detects frustration, it transfers to a human agent with full conversation context intact, per Tidio's own Lyro documentation and third-party reviews (eesel AI, tidio.com/blog/lyro-review).
Internal notes with @mentions (invisible to customers) and chat/ticket assignment to specific agents or departments are documented features (help.tidio.com, Internal notes and mentions).
Macros let agents insert reusable messages/links in chats, tickets, and internal notes, and can trigger actions like re-assignment, tagging, or status changes (help.tidio.com, Macros article).

Lyro can look up real Shopify order status after verifying the customer (email + order ID), and agents can cancel orders, submit refunds, and edit shipping addresses directly from the dashboard — refunds require the Growth plan (help.tidio.com, Manage Shopify orders / Shopify FAQ).

The native WooCommerce integration sends product cards in chat and syncs customer/lead data with real-time click tracking, but lacks the documented order-lookup/refund depth Shopify has; deeper automation runs through a separate Zapier bridge (tidio.com/integrations/woocommerce, Zapier app page).
Tidio ships an official WordPress plugin (wordpress.org/plugins/tidio-live-chat) as part of its 120+ platform integrations, installed like a standard plugin rather than a manual script embed.

As of September 30, 2024, the Tidio Live Chat & AI Chatbots app is no longer distributed through the Wix App Market; installation now requires manually pasting custom code via Settings > Advanced > Custom Code, and pre-existing Wix-originated accounts had to migrate to keep premium plans (help.tidio.com Install Tidio on Wix, corroborated by third-party sources).
Squarespace support is a manual JavaScript snippet pasted into Settings > Advanced > Code Injection Footer, not a dedicated app/plugin (help.tidio.com, Install Tidio on Squarespace).

Webflow support is likewise a single JavaScript snippet embed rather than a native app, with deeper workflow sync (e.g., contact data) requiring a separate Zapier connection (webflow.com/integrations/tidio).

Tidio has a dedicated Zapier integration with triggers for new contacts/bot events (zapier.com/apps/tidio/integrations), but no dedicated native Make.com or n8n integration surfaced in Tidio's own docs — those would rely on generic webhooks instead.

Tidio has documented native integrations for HubSpot (lead capture/sync), Salesforce (contact and conversation sync), and Pipedrive (contact export plus one-click deal creation from chats) (tidio.com/integrations/category/crm, tidio.com/integrations/pipedrive).

Lyro pulls live order data from Shopify (not scripted talk) after identity verification, and agents can act on it directly — cancel, refund, or edit shipping — per Tidio's Shopify order-management documentation.

Lyro auto-detects the customer's language mid-conversation and replies natively in that language (not via translation) across 48 supported languages, and the chat widget separately auto-detects browser language (help.tidio.com, Lyro Multilanguage support).

The Analytics section covers interactions, Lyro resolution rate, sales assisted, leads acquired, live conversations, tickets, agent performance, and online hours, plus CSAT surveys after chats/tickets (help.tidio.com, The Analytics section) — solid but some independent comparisons note it falls short of dedicated CX platforms' deeper AI-driven analytics.

Billing is split across three separate quotas (billable conversations, Lyro AI conversations, Flow triggers), and Trustpilot reviews repeatedly describe being auto-upgraded to pricier plans without clear consent and struggling to get refunds (trustpilot.com/review/www.tidio.com, current rating 3.8/5 with a notable share of 1-star reviews).

Tidio offers OpenAPI, webhooks, and a Widget SDK via developers.tidio.com, but webhooks are gated to the Plus and Premium plans only, per Tidio's own developer documentation (help.tidio.com, Use Webhooks in Tidio).

scorecard.note: Consistently the top-praised attribute across independent reviews — live chat and AI chat are reported ready with minimal setup effort.
Reviewers report roughly 90% resolution rates with minimal hallucination, a strong independent signal, though the Lyro-vs-scripted-bot rigidity is a real design limitation.
Solid on web chat, email, and core social DMs, but narrower channel coverage than platforms like Crisp or ManyChat.
Reasonable entry pricing, but pricing transparency — unexpected upgrades and refund friction — is the most repeated complaint in independent reviews.
Support is described as responsive, friendly, and quick to resolve setup issues in the large majority of reviews.

pricing.model: Tiered helpdesk plans by billable conversations, plus separate add-on billing for Lyro AI and Flows

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 50 billable conversations, 10 seats, live chat, ticketing, email management

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: 100 billable conversations, 10 seats, 50 Lyro AI conversations (one-off), 100 Flows visitors

plans.name: Growth
plans.notes: Up to 2,000 billable conversations, 10 seats, advanced analytics, automatic chat assignment, macros, permissions

plans.name: Lyro AI Agent (add-on)
plans.notes: 50+ Lyro conversations, sold separately from the core helpdesk plan

pricingBreakdown: Tidio splits its bill into two separate decisions: the core helpdesk (Free through Growth at $49.17/mo, priced by billable conversations and seats) and Lyro AI, billed separately starting at $32.50/mo for just 50 AI conversations. That split is the single thing to budget around — a team that signs up for Growth at $49.17/mo thinking that's the whole bill will be surprised when Lyro costs land as a second, independent charge, and $32.50/mo for 50 conversations is a notably worse per-conversation rate than Crisp's Mini plan, where $45/mo buys both 4 seats and roughly 90 automated AI conversations bundled together. Where Tidio's pricing does make real sense is the Free tier: unlike Chatbase's Free tier, which is genuinely a stripped-down trial, Tidio's Free plan ships real ticketing and email management alongside live chat for 10 seats — that's usable production software, not a demo. If Lyro's ~90% independently-reported resolution rate holds for your use case, paying the AI add-on separately is a fair trade for accuracy; if you're price-sensitive and mostly want bundled AI-plus-inbox in one number, Crisp's per-workspace bundling is simply the easier bill to forecast.

capabilities.note: Lyro is the headline feature, and the independently-reported ~90% resolution rate with minimal hallucination is a genuinely strong signal — not a vendor claim, an outside one. The real design limitation worth knowing before you buy: you can't smoothly blend a simple scripted bot with intelligent Lyro handoff in one flow, it's a binary choice between Flows (rule-based) and the full AI agent, which reviewers specifically flag as a rigidity they'd fix if they could.

The chat widget and AI agent both get consistent praise for being ready with minimal setup — this is the most-praised attribute across independent reviews, and it's not a close second. If setup speed is a real priority, Tidio is one of the fastest options on this list to get a working live chat and AI combination in front of customers.

Ticketing and email management are bundled into the core plan even at Free, with automatic chat assignment and macros arriving at Growth ($49.17/mo). This is a real inbox, not a stripped trial version — the Free tier alone covers more ground than some competitors' entry-level paid plans.

Lyro trains on your website, uploaded documents, CSV files, and even Zendesk help center articles if you're migrating from that platform. It's functional as a training source for the AI rather than a standalone customer-facing knowledge base product, so don't expect a dedicated help-center builder here.

This is the honest weak spot: independent hands-on review specifically notes Tidio has no real marketing capability on Facebook, Instagram, or WhatsApp beyond basic auto-replies. If proactive, cross-channel campaign broadcasting matters to you, this isn't the tool for it — Tidio's strength is reactive support, not outbound marketing.

pros: Genuinely fast setup — live chat and AI agent both reported ready with minimal configuration effort
Strong independent AI-quality signal: ~90% resolution rate with minimal hallucination reported by reviewers
Free tier includes real helpdesk functionality (ticketing, email management), not just a stripped demo
Responsive, well-regarded customer support across the large majority of reviews
cons: Pricing transparency is the most-repeated complaint — automatic plan upgrades and refund friction appear across many independent reviews
Rigid separation between scripted bots (Flows) and the full Lyro AI agent, with no smooth intelligent handoff between the two
Lyro AI Agent is billed as a separate add-on from the core helpdesk plan, complicating total-cost estimation
Narrower channel coverage (no native WhatsApp, SMS, or voice) compared to Crisp or ManyChat

sentiment.quote: Tidio was incredibly easy to set up and customise...the chatbot builder is intuitive and flexible.
sentiment.source: Capterra (Carl R., Managing Director, Financial Services)

sentiment.quote: The interface is smooth and user-friendly, and the free version already covers the essentials.
After joining the Tidio Partner Program, I was promised a free upgrade but never received a reply.
sentiment.source: Capterra (Calvin J., Marketer, Marketing and Advertising)

bestFor: E-commerce and small-to-mid-sized business websites wanting fast live chat plus AI resolution
Teams that want a real free tier with ticketing and email, not just a chat-widget trial
Businesses comfortable budgeting Lyro AI conversations separately from the core helpdesk plan
Support teams prioritizing setup speed and AI accuracy over deep omnichannel breadth
verdict: Tidio earns its strong review average honestly, not through review-gating tricks — the roughly 90% Lyro resolution rate with minimal hallucination that reviewers report independently is a genuinely strong signal, and setup speed rivals Chatbase's best-in-class time-to-launch. The rub is the pricing structure, and it's a real one: splitting the core helpdesk plan from Lyro AI billing means a team budgeting $49.17/mo for Growth gets blindsided when the AI add-on lands as a separate charge on top, starting at $32.50/mo for just 50 conversations — a worse per-conversation rate than what Crisp bundles into its Mini plan for roughly the same money. The recurring complaints about surprise plan upgrades and refund friction are specific and numerous enough across independent reviews that I'd take them seriously before entering card details, not wave them off as the usual noise every SaaS product collects. Where Tidio genuinely makes sense: an e-commerce store that wants AI doing the heavy lifting fast and is comfortable budgeting the AI line item separately from the base plan. Where it doesn't: if you need WhatsApp or voice alongside your chat — that's simply not in Tidio's channel lineup no matter which tier you pick, so no amount of budget fixes that gap.
